1.8.verification: The diagnostic exercises are examples, not a measured ranking of the ten most common errors.

2.1.label: Inspect build settings → Locate isolation boundary → Apply minimal correction → Compile and exercise
2.1.verification: The local concurrency fixture has recorded static before/after findings; it is not proof that one setting fixes every migration.

2.2.label: Tool event → Hook handler → Exit status → Continue or stop
2.2.verification: Claude script-level checks and Muse Stop discovery have different scopes. Full cross-client enforcement remains unverified.

2.3.label: Choose state → Navigate deterministically → Capture screen → Compare criterion
2.3.verification: The baseline screenshot proves an empty screen was visible; it does not prove persistence or VoiceOver navigation.

2.4.label: Inspect scope → Review risky boundaries → Run focused checks → Accept or revise
2.4.verification: This is a review procedure, not a guaranteed five-minute duration.

2.5.label: Clean baseline → New branch or worktree → Small reviewed change → Test then integrate
2.5.verification: The workflow is source guidance; a four-client isolation experiment is not claimed.

2.6.label: Primitive palette → Semantic roles → Component usage → Appearance checks
2.6.verification: Generated asset structure has evidence; visual quality still needs checks in the actual app.

2.7.label: Choose one behavior → Supply project context → Request bounded change → Inspect result
2.7.verification: The prompts below are practice prompts, not 25 completed comparative runs.

2.8.label: Expected behavior → Actual output → Reproduction → Bounded conclusion
2.8.verification: No evidence supports a universal list of ten things agents cannot do; the lesson teaches failure classification instead.

3.1.label: View model → Store protocol → SwiftData adapter → Relaunch verification
3.1.verification: The Reading List acceptance suite does not verify a SwiftData migration.

3.2.label: Stored collection → Search query → Filtered result → Clear to recover
3.2.verification: Reading List contains corresponding checks; a full accessibility audit is a separate task.

3.3.label: Request → Validate response → Decode model → Publish current result
3.3.verification: This chapter's networking exercise is not a new recorded network integration test.

3.4.label: User action or URL → Validated route → Navigation state → Destination
3.4.verification: The source guide supplies patterns; no blanket claim is made that a navigation review catches every routing bug.

3.5.label: Shared snapshot → Timeline entry → Widget view → Intent-triggered change
3.5.verification: The installed Xcode 26.6 cannot verify iOS 27-only widget styling; that lab is blocked.

3.6.label: User request → Intent parameters → Domain operation → Result and presentation
3.6.verification: Do not infer Siri behavior from a static review or claim new SDK deprecations without checking Apple documentation.

3.7.label: SDK guard → Runtime readiness → Model session → Useful fallback
3.7.verification: A simulator or static sample cannot establish every supported physical-device model configuration.

3.8.label: User permission → Register capability → Schedule work → Handle expiration
3.8.verification: A source review cannot prove that the operating system will schedule a task at a specific time.

3.9.label: Incoming URL → Validate fields → Resolve route → Render state
3.9.verification: Custom URL routing and universal-link association are different checks; one does not validate the other.

3.10.label: Source string → Context and placeholders → Translation review → Layout checks
3.10.verification: Machine-generated translations still need language review; no multi-language audit is claimed.

4.1.label: Layer sources → Composite preview → Catalog asset → Device inspection
4.1.verification: A PNG export is not automatically a native Icon Composer bundle or App Review approval.

4.2.label: Explicit tokens → Validate names → Generate catalog → Compile and inspect
4.2.verification: The existing asset walkthrough includes actool evidence; it does not establish contrast in every screen.

4.3.label: Semantic text style → Scaled content → Flexible layout → Largest-size check
4.3.verification: Source examples are guidance; screenshots and VoiceOver checks must come from the actual app.

4.4.label: User action → State change → Motion preference → Appropriate feedback
4.4.verification: No physical-device haptic evaluation is included in the simulator baseline.

4.5.label: Task hierarchy → Content and controls → Tokens and spacing → State review
4.5.verification: The pattern library is a starting point, not evidence that a particular redesign improved usability.

4.6.label: Select device → Seed safe content → Navigate state → Capture and inspect
4.6.verification: The baseline screenshot is demonstration evidence, not a complete App Store screenshot set.

4.7.label: Design variables → Semantic token mapping → Asset catalog → SwiftUI usage
4.7.verification: No live Figma import session was run; this is the supported handoff contract, not a custom parser.

5.1.label: Behavior contract → Test layer → Controlled dependency → Assertion
5.1.verification: Apple documents coexistence; no complete project migration is claimed here.

5.2.label: Launch isolated state → Perform action → Wait for condition → Assert outcome
5.2.verification: The Reading List suite provides concrete UI coverage; it does not prove the absence of all flakes.

5.3.label: Semantic labels → Navigation order → Adaptive layout → Device review
5.3.verification: A successful UI test is not a complete VoiceOver audit.

5.4.label: Reproduce workload → Record baseline → Change one cause → Compare trace
5.4.verification: No invented launch-time or hang-rate numbers are supplied.

5.5.label: Owner → Stored closure or subscription → Captured owner → Break intended edge
5.5.verification: Static review findings require runtime confirmation when lifetime depends on navigation or cancellation.

5.6.label: Sensitive input → Storage boundary → Network boundary → Redacted diagnostics
5.6.verification: This checklist is not a penetration test or a guarantee of security.

5.7.label: Static finding → Inspect context → Compile → Exercise behavior
5.7.verification: Do not count a suppressed warning as a repaired defect.

6.1.label: Working build → Privacy and metadata → Signed archive → Submission review
6.1.verification: No app was submitted to App Review for this series.

6.2.verification: Current Apple requirements must be checked for the actual release; this is not legal advice or submission approval.

6.3.label: Local acceptance → Distribution configuration → Upload build → Tester feedback
6.3.verification: No TestFlight upload is authorized or performed in this series; the end-to-end lab is blocked.

6.4.label: Review message → Relevant behavior → Small correction → Resubmission evidence
6.4.verification: No sourced rejection case collection has been assembled; no invented rejection stories are presented.

6.5.label: Changes since tag → User-facing behavior → Version consistency → Release notes
6.5.verification: This writing task does not authorize a new npm release.

6.6.label: Checkout → Install pinned dependencies → Build and test → Report failures
6.6.verification: A workflow file is not a successful run; inspect the actual job result.

7.8.verification: Existing records are dated snapshots, not guarantees for later versions.

8.1.label: Requirement → Finding location → Context → Minimal patch
8.1.verification: A review-first prompt is a technique, not a measured universal quality gain.

8.2.verification: No evidence supports the original claim that one prompt fixes half of all concurrency errors.

8.3.label: Named state → Reproduction steps → Capture → Compare
8.3.verification: A screenshot is visual evidence, not proof of every behavior.

8.4.label: Recorded toolchain → API choice → Build → Availability review
8.4.verification: Do not label an API available solely because it appears in a newer guide.

8.5.label: Validated URL → Seeded item → Destination → Screenshot
8.5.verification: Not every screen should expose a public route; keep test hooks appropriately scoped.

8.6.label: Token source → Named asset → View use → Appearance check
8.6.verification: Centralized tokens do not guarantee contrast or visual quality.

8.7.label: Spec change → Generator → Project diff → Build
8.7.verification: Do not regenerate with an unrecorded tool version or overwrite unrelated manual changes.

8.8.label: API introduction → Deployment target → Runtime readiness → Fallback
8.8.verification: Text-based guard checks cannot model every control-flow path.

8.9.label: Lifecycle event → Handler → Exit status → Explain result
8.9.verification: Hook schemas and exit behavior are client-specific; copying JSON does not verify dispatch.

8.10.label: Completion claim → Exact command → Fresh result → Accept or reopen
8.10.verification: Passing selected tests does not prove untested paths.

8.11.label: One goal → Small diff → Acceptance check → Checkpoint
8.11.verification: Small work units can still require careful integration testing.

8.12.label: Code task → Need account change? → Explicit review → Local configuration
8.12.verification: An absolute ban is not necessary for every authorized workflow; secret values still stay out of chat and source.

8.13.label: Claim → Supporting artifact → Missing check → Follow-up
8.13.verification: Wording alone cannot prove deception or correctness; inspect the evidence.

8.14.label: Failure → Minimal fixture → Negative case → Review rule
8.14.verification: Do not upload private app code to build a public fixture.

8.15.label: Feature claim → Official schema → Controlled failure → Observed response
8.15.verification: Observer enablement instructions are blocked until verified; no setting is guessed.

8.16.label: Shared baseline → Separate checkout → Independent task → Reviewed integration
8.16.verification: Resolve shared simulator and data-store ownership separately.

8.17.label: Start build → Retain logs → Wait for completion → Inspect exit status
8.17.verification: Antigravity background-subagent behavior is unverified here, so no client-specific command is provided.

8.18.label: Inspect files → Identify dependencies → Agree criteria → Edit one slice
8.18.verification: Planning does not itself validate implementation or guarantee lower cost.

8.19.label: Focused local search → Read source section → Identify gap → Check primary source
8.19.verification: A local catalog is dated and is not Apple's proprietary framework implementation.

8.20.label: Classify file → Source or generated? → Ignore narrowly → Inspect git status
8.20.verification: Ignoring a secret after committing it does not remove it from history.
